title: Drone
subtitle: the ones who only know one job
narrative: Kaladesh's design brief named cogwork automatons 'ambient infrastructure' inside a five-stage caste called the Aether Cycle. Clockwork Servant's flavor speaker is uncredited: the castle custodians who find the ticking sweet are the ones not cleaning the cobbles. A pop idol cosplaying as the boss of a factory floor, illustrated by an artist who once said he was 'obsessed with Magic: The Gathering' four years before Wizards absorbed his franchise. Nineteen cards, twelve names, four games. Curated as labor.

cards.name: Hatsune Miku "Factory Tyrant"
cards.image_cache_reason: Bushiroad's en.ws-tcg.com CDN serves all free card images with a giant diagonal SAMPLE watermark (unusable on a buyer-facing storefront) AND sends x-content-type-options:nosniff without Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy (Chrome ORB blocks it as a no-cors image). TCGplayer's product-images CDN hosts the clean unwatermarked scan at product ID 106389. Cached locally.
cards.why_it_fits: Headline of the bundle. The Project DIVA Factory Tyrant module's costume was designed by cosMo@BousouP himself — atypical for SEGA, who normally handles modules in-house. He composed the song too: 'Sadistic Music Infinity Factory,' which casts Miku as a tyrannical plant manager demanding an unending supply of music or she goes insane. The most-produced character in pop culture, cosplaying as the person who runs the place that produces things.

cards.name: Phyrexian Ironworks
cards.why_it_fits: Flavor speaker is Slobad the Mirran goblin engineer. In Fifth Dawn, Memnarch amputated his limbs and wired him into a spark-transfer machine for five years — he was the involuntary architect of the device meant to strip Mirrodin's inhabitants of their sparks. He sacrificed the spark, was later killed, compleated by Phyrexia, and reshaped his Phyrexian body to resemble his dead friend Bosh. 'We have made a friend today' reads as either propaganda or broken optimism.

cards.name: Workshop Assistant
cards.why_it_fits: First printed on Kaladesh, where the official Aether Cycle five-stage caste designated dwarves as the Build phase — the labor layer that maintains everyone else's inventions. The Countless Gears guild specialized in 'the smallest automatons and thopters'; the spider-form fits their profile exactly. Pairs with Junk Diver in a documented infinite combo at common rarity (Pauper-legal). 'Sometimes the smallest things make the biggest difference.' The assistant exists to be consumed so the workshop keeps running.

cards.name: Will-Forged Golem
cards.why_it_fits: Convoke lets your other creatures tap to help pay the cost — the golem is built by everyone you already had on board, the way real factories work. M15 changed Convoke from cost-reduction to alternative-cost payment, expanded it from green-white to all five colors and artifacts. Artist Jason Felix was suspended by Wizards in 2021 after admitting he'd lifted other artists' work in a Strixhaven commission. A card about consensual collective labor, painted by someone the institution defunded for stealing it.

cards.name: Clockwork Servant
cards.why_it_fits: Eldraine castle infrastructure. Flavor speaker is uncredited — 'to the castle custodians, there's no sweeter sound' belongs to whoever's not cleaning the cobbles. Direct lineage to Clockwork Gnomes (Homelands 1995), flavor by Baki the Wizard Attendant: 'Until I came to the Floating Isle, I never had to oil the servants.' Twenty-four years of mechanical-servant logic, unchanged. Adamant lets it work for any court.

cards.name: Iron Bully
cards.why_it_fits: Flavor speaker Commander Grozdan is a confirmed named character: Boros minotaur, Ordruun bloodline, Kamen Fortress anti-Rakdos enforcer per the Guildmasters' Guide to Ravnica (2018). Mid-invasion: 'Why would someone have built ... wait, never mind. Send it to the front lines!' The Boros officer's question about why the object exists is interrupted by his own order to deploy it. Manufacture and use, no gap.

cards.name: Yotian Soldier
cards.why_it_fits: Antiquities-era Urza memorial. After the Fall of Kroog he mass-produced these as lighter defensive units — a guilt project in volume. The Battlebond reprint strips the eulogy flavor. Brothers' War (2022) introduced four new Yotian-named cards but cut a Yotian Soldier reprint, per Rosewater, because the retro artifact bonus sheet covered it. Same illustrator (Luca Zontini) also painted Skullclamp — the humblest defensive common and MTG's most aggressively-banned equipment, one hand.

cards.name: Klang
cards.why_it_fits: Ken Sugimori's design brief: 'something inorganic.' Among the first Pokemon Game Freak built as purely mechanical, not animals with metallic traits — the Klink line was in the eye of Gen 5's 'Object Pokemon' design controversy. The Black 2 Pokedex death entry: 'if the minigear it launches at a foe doesn't return, it will die.' The TCG flavor text reads the same mechanic as a feature: spec sheet on one side, mortality on the other.

cards.name: Drone Rotom
cards.why_it_fits: Rotom's five battling forms possess household appliances — oven, fridge, fan, lawnmower, washing machine. The Drone form is a sixth, non-battling: Rotom inhabits drones to film live Gym Challenge matches at Wyndon Stadium. The TCG card is a Trainer Item, not a creature — canonically the correct product category. Five Drone Rotom formed the World Coronation Series logo in smoke above Wyndon in JN115, the anime's 1,200th episode. Ghost made employee.

cards.name: Golem
cards.why_it_fits: From Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Echoes of Time, a 2009 DS/Wii spin-off that sold ~570K and was outsold by Persona 4: Golden. Common rarity, species name as card name. Artist Yasuhisa Izumisawa, in a 2019 Square Enix interview: 'For a while, I was obsessed with Magic: The Gathering. A lot of money and long nights went into playing that game.' In 2025 Wizards absorbed Final Fantasy into Universes Beyond — highest-grossing MTG set ever, $200M day one. The FFTCG artist was a Magic player before Magic ate his franchise.

cards.name: Eldrazi Repurposer
cards.why_it_fits: Type line literally reads 'Creature — Eldrazi Drone.' Flavor speaker General Tazri led the allied resistance against Ulamog: 'I almost admire their ability to avoid waste. Almost.' The bundle's thesis spoken by a soldier looking at the workforce that's going to eat her. MH3 deliberately reverted from Scion tokens to Spawn tokens — per Rosewater, 0/1 Spawns suit higher-powered sets where the mana ability is the draw. Three copies in this lair: production-line repurposers come in batches.

cards.name: Henge Walker
cards.why_it_fits: Animated by the wild magic flowing through the Great Henge — a structure giants built on Eldraine before humans rose, and a magical gateway between the Realm and the Wilds. The Great Henge card sits at $63.89 today. Henge Walker sits at six cents. Same location, two outputs, ~1000x price gap. Artist Titus Lunter was detained at Sea-Tac by ICE in 2018 while flying to Wizards HQ for D&D concept work — deported, ESTA permanently revoked, no public Wizards statement.

pricing.diy_shipping_rate_note: $1.31 matches TCGplayer's standard Plain Envelope rate as of 2026-05-17; Weiss Schwarz singles route through TCGplayer as well, same rate applies.
pricing.diy_alternative_note: Nineteen cards across twelve names, ten sets, four games (Weiss Schwarz Project DIVA, MH3, Commander Legends, M15, Throne of Eldraine, War of the Spark, Battlebond, Darkness Ablaze, Vivid Voltage, FFTCG Opus VIII). Realistically routes through 7 TCGplayer sellers minimum at $1.31 plain-envelope shipping each. The Hatsune Miku Weiss Schwarz card and the FFTCG Golem each tend to ship from format-specialist sellers separate from the MTG/Pokemon supply chain; the 4-of Henge Walker and 3-of Eldrazi Repurposer often split across two sellers each.
pricing.shipping_policy: buyer-paid, itemized separately at checkout; never included in list price
pricing.shipping_rate_note: Matches TCGplayer Plain Envelope rate ($1.31). One envelope, one stamp; we eat the difference if the carrier's actual stamp cost runs over.
pricing.premium_justification: Nineteen cards across twelve names, weighted heavily on the Hatsune Miku 'Factory Tyrant' Double Rare ($11). The bundle leans into multi-copy depth where inventory supports it: four Henge Walkers, three Eldrazi Repurposers, two each of Phyrexian Ironworks and Klang. Doing this DIY across seven sellers at $1.31 plain-envelope shipping each runs $22.29; this lair arrives in one envelope for $18.00 + $1.31. You save $4.29 versus DIY (19%). The premium pays for the curation: the cross-franchise thesis is the product, not the cards individually. A buyer who wanted nineteen production-line workers across MTG and Pokemon and FFTCG and Weiss Schwarz would not search this way; the assembly is the labor being sold.

metadata.notes: EXAMPLE bundle for buyer-facing showcase. NOT a real inventory claim: no card MDs were modified, no held_for_lair counters incremented, no card bundles[] field updated. Headline anchor is Hatsune Miku 'Factory Tyrant' PD/S22-E027 RR ($11 market) as the visual + narrative crown of the production-line cohort; supporting cast is MTG bulk constructs/golems plus Pokemon mechanical-creature staples plus an FFTCG genre-representative Golem. The 'status: example' enum is introduced here to distinguish from proposed/accepted/assembled bundles in the lifecycle.
